headline: Up to 142% hike: Cabinet approves ninth pay scale for govt employees
summary: The new National Pay Scale 2026 will see basic salaries increase by 100-142%, with the lowest grade receiving the highest percentage jump.
details: The Cabinet has approved the ninth pay scale for government employees, redefining basic salaries while maintaining the existing 20 pay grades.
Under the new structure, the maximum basic salary for Grade-1 will be set at 156,000 BDT, while the minimum basic salary for the 20th Grade will be 20,000 BDT.
The ratio between the lowest and highest grade salaries has been reduced from 1:1.945 to 1:1.78, leading to a significant increase for lower-grade employees.
As a result, the basic salary for the lowest grade will increase by 142%, while the highest grade will see a 100% increase.
The new pay scale will take effect from July 1 of this year. The basic salary increases will be implemented in three phases by July 1, 2027.
Allowances will become effective from January 1, 2028.
caption:
Government employees are set for a massive pay jump! The new 9th pay scale is approved, with basic salaries rising by up to 142%.

The ratio between the lowest and highest grade salaries has been reduced from 1:1.945 to 1:1.78, leading to a significant increase for lower-grade employees.

As a result, the basic salary for the lowest grade will increase by 142%, while the highest grade will see a 100% increase.

The new pay scale will take effect from July 1 of this year. The basic salary increases will be implemented in three phases by July 1, 2027.

headline_marked: 1,163 hospitalised: [[4 die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 1,163 hospitalised: 4 die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The number of hospitalisations in a single day has reached a record high as the national death toll rises to 97.
details: At least four dengue patients died and 1,163 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am this morning.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), this marks the highest number of hospitalisations recorded in a single day.
Of the latest deaths, two occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, one in Dhaka North City Corporation, and one in Mymensingh division.
With these new additions, the total number of dengue cases in the country has reached 35,846, while the death toll has risen to 97.
Currently, 2,544 dengue patients are receiving treatment at hospitals across the country.
